_why: One business rule written by hand in more than one file. Declare it once here; tools/run shared-rules then does two passes — compare (the copies disagree) and discover (a file uses the rule and is not listed).

_example.statement: A question renders as a dropdown only when it has MORE than DROPDOWN_MIN_OPTIONS options — strictly greater, not >=. The only screen that obeys it is the participant's, which is why a second copy with >= survived for months.
_notes: mustMatch names a SHAPE, not a value. A bare "'MULTIPLE'" is satisfied by an unrelated array 300 lines away, so deleting the rule from the function it guards would change nothing — the tool refuses such patterns.

kind 'mention' asks which file NAMES the symbol — right for a threshold or a tab order with few legitimate mentions. kind 'declaration' asks which file DECLARES it — right for an enum that many honest consumers import, where 'mention' would return twenty files and tempt you into nineteen useless exceptions.
